solutionSql:
SELECT s.id AS shipment_id
FROM shipments s
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM shipment_events e
    WHERE e.shipment_id = s.id AND e.status = 'delivered'
  )
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM invoices i
    WHERE i.shipment_id = s.id
  )
ORDER BY shipment_id;

rules.howSolved: Two EXISTS checks on the shipment: one for a shipment_events row with status 'delivered', one for an invoices row, so both are required.

ambiguities: The instruction says 'shipment' without naming the source table. I took shipment_id from shipments. Taking it from shipment_events gives identical rows on sample, nulls and ties, because those datasets have no orphan scans or invoices.
The status literal 'delivered' is matched exactly. The sample statuses are all lowercase.
notes: Sample returns 21 rows. A shipment_events-based formulation returns the same rows on sample, nulls and ties. Orphan counts are 0 on those datasets.
